Rows a size-proportional design takes with certainty

Source: R/inclusion.R
certainty_set.Rd

A design whose inclusion probabilities are proportional to size gives a row whose share of n reaches 1 a probability of exactly 1, and spreads what is left of n over the other rows, repeating until no share passes

  1. certainty_set() says which rows of data those are, and where the cut-off falls, before any sample is drawn.

Usage

certainty_set(data, design)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

design

design_weighted() with method = "systematic" or "poisson", or design_spread() with a size column. Other designs are refused, since none of them has inclusion probabilities proportional to size.

Value

An integer vector of the rows of data whose inclusion probability is 1, in frame order, the same rows as which(inclusion_prob(data, design) == 1). Its attribute threshold is the smallest size among them, or NA when there are none. Of the rows the design can select, those whose size is at least threshold are the set. With strata, design_weighted() and design_spread() put the cut-off in each stratum at its own size, so there threshold is NA. For design_weighted() without strata, design_certainty() with that threshold on the weights column therefore takes the same rows with certainty, and a rest of the same method with n reduced by the number of rows in the set gives the other rows the same probabilities too.

See also

inclusion_prob(), design_certainty()

Examples

df <- data.frame(id = 1:10, w = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 60, 90))
d <- design_weighted("w", n = 4, method = "systematic")
cs <- certainty_set(df, d)
df[cs, ]
#>    id  w
#> 9   9 60
#> 10 10 90
attr(cs, "threshold")
#> [1] 60

# The same probabilities, with the cut-off made explicit
same <- design_certainty("w", attr(cs, "threshold"),
                         rest = design_weighted("w", n = 4 - length(cs),
                                                method = "systematic"))
all.equal(inclusion_prob(df, same), inclusion_prob(df, d))
#> [1] TRUE
